title: System Design
description: Real-world enterprise system design prompts as they appear in Turing FDE, Andela senior, and Toptal advanced rounds. Each has a rubric — self-score against it after drafting your answer aloud.

questions.prompt: Design a rate limiter supporting BOTH per-user (100 req/min) AND global (10k req/min) limits, running across N application nodes.

rubric.criterion: Asks about consistency guarantees (strict vs lax), latency budget, and cost tolerance
Proposes token bucket or leaky bucket (with rationale)
Uses shared store (Redis with atomic Lua script or INCR+EXPIRE) to synchronize across nodes
Handles clock skew, race conditions on refill, and Redis outage
Returns 429 with Retry-After header and rate-limit response headers
Discusses per-endpoint tiering and how to introduce new limits without downtime

questions.modelAnswer: Token bucket per key. State in Redis: HASH { tokens, last_refill_ts } per user_id and a global key. Refill using Lua script for atomic read-modify-write. On each request: refill both buckets, decrement if ≥1 else 429. Retry-After = ceil((1 - tokens)/refill_rate). Fallback if Redis is down: in-memory local limit with generous headroom + circuit breaker. For fan-out sanity, per-user key TTL after inactivity.

questions.prompt: Design a private, VPC-deployed RAG system for a healthcare customer with HIPAA constraints and 50M documents.

rubric.criterion: Clarifies: doc types, refresh rate, latency SLO, expected QPS, retention/PHI rules
All components in customer VPC — self-hosted embedding model + vector DB + inference; no data leaves the boundary
Ingestion pipeline: chunk (semantic or fixed) → embed → store with metadata; incremental re-embed on updates
Retrieval: ANN (HNSW/IVF) + BM25 hybrid; reranker; metadata filters; retrieval eval offline
Guardrails: PII redaction pre-embed, output PHI check, audit log of every query + retrieved docs
Access control: user attributes cascade into filter (RBAC/ABAC); no cross-tenant leakage
Observability + evaluation: precision@k, faithfulness, human review loop

questions.modelAnswer: Deploy on customer's AWS via CloudFormation. S3 (SSE-KMS) for source docs → Lambda triggers on put → SageMaker endpoint for embedding (self-hosted sentence-transformers or BGE) → OpenSearch (or pgvector) for hybrid retrieval. Inference: vLLM/TGI hosting a self-hosted LLM (Llama or medical-fine-tuned). Kong/API Gateway with per-role JWT. Presidio for PII scrub. CloudWatch + S3 audit trail. Ground-truth eval set curated with clinicians for precision + faithfulness monitoring.

questions.prompt: Design a reliable webhook integration with a client system that frequently goes offline.

rubric.criterion: At-least-once delivery + idempotency key so retries are safe
Exponential backoff with jitter and a max retry window
Dead-letter queue for terminal failures with alerting + replay tool
Signed payloads (HMAC + timestamp) so client can verify authenticity + block replays
Delivery persistence (outbox pattern) so events survive service restarts
Backpressure/throttling per endpoint to avoid overloading recovering clients

questions.modelAnswer: Outbox in the same DB txn that produced the event. Worker reads outbox → PUT to client URL with X-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 over body + ts) and X-Idempotency-Key. On non-2xx, requeue with exp backoff (1s, 4s, 15s, 1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 6h, cap 24h). After N failures → DLQ + alert. Small circuit breaker per endpoint to pause after repeated failures. Dashboard for redelivery.

questions.prompt: Design an integration between a client CRM using OAuth 1.0 and your platform using OAuth 2.0.

rubric.criterion: Names both protocols correctly and identifies the bridging service as the boundary
Bridge stores client OAuth 1.0 tokens + secret encrypted at rest per user
Signs outbound requests with HMAC-SHA1 + nonce + timestamp for OAuth 1.0
Client-side uses OAuth 2.0 Auth Code + PKCE to obtain platform tokens
Token rotation, refresh handling, and re-consent flow when tokens expire or scopes change
Audit log + revoke path for compliance

questions.modelAnswer: Introduce an Adapter Service. Users log in to our platform via OAuth 2.0 (with PKCE). During onboarding, redirect through OAuth 1.0 flow to CRM: request-token → user authorizes → access-token. Encrypt (KMS) and store the CRM tokens keyed by our user id. Adapter signs OAuth 1.0 requests per RFC 5849 whenever CRM API is called. Health check + refresh flow. Revocation endpoint invalidates stored tokens.

questions.prompt: Design a monitoring system for a multi-tenant SaaS where each client has different SLA requirements (99%, 99.9%, 99.99%).

rubric.criterion: Isolates per-tenant metrics (labels/tags) end-to-end
SLO-based alerting: error budget consumption per tenant, not just raw thresholds
Multi-window burn-rate alerts to avoid noisy false positives
Per-tenant dashboards + customer-facing status page
Data-retention tiering per tier (99.99% keeps longer, higher-resolution)
Incident routing to the right on-call based on tenant tier

questions.modelAnswer: Prometheus (or Datadog) with tenant_id label on every metric. Define SLIs (availability, latency P95, error rate) per tenant. SLOs stored as YAML per tier. Sloth or Pyrra to generate burn-rate alert rules. Grafana per-tenant dashboards + external status page via Statuspage.io. Alertmanager routes by tier → PagerDuty escalation policy per tier.

questions.prompt: Design a distributed job queue with priorities, retries, and dead-letter handling.

rubric.criterion: Chooses backing store (Redis/BullMQ, SQS+DLQ, or Kafka) with rationale
Priority mechanism (per-priority queues OR weighted scheduling)
Retry with exp backoff, max attempts, then DLQ
Idempotent job handlers via idempotency key
Worker scaling (concurrency + auto-scaling on queue depth)
Observability: age of oldest message, throughput, failure rate

questions.modelAnswer: Redis + BullMQ. Multiple named queues (critical/normal/low) each with its own worker pool sized by SLA. Each job has jobId (dedup) + idempotency-safe handler. Retry: 5 attempts, exp backoff. Terminal fail → DLQ + Slack alert. Autoscale workers via KEDA on queue length. Prometheus exporter for age/throughput. Nightly job to reap zombie locks.

questions.prompt: Design ingestion + transformation for 12 fragmented retail data sources into a forecasting model.

rubric.criterion: Classifies each source (batch vs stream, structured vs semi-structured, refresh)
Landing zone (raw layer) → cleaned/silver → aggregated/gold pattern
Schema-on-read for messy sources; contracts on the gold layer
Orchestration (Airflow/Dagster/dbt) + observability of pipeline SLAs
Data quality: freshness, volume, distribution checks; alert on drift
Backfill + reprocessing story for corrections

questions.modelAnswer: S3 raw zone partitioned by source/date. Fivetran + custom Airbyte connectors ingest each source (or Kafka Connect for streaming). dbt transforms to silver (cleaned) then gold (per-SKU per-day features). Airflow DAG orchestrates dependencies. Great Expectations for DQ. Feature store (Feast) feeds the model. Backfills: idempotent DAGs keyed by logical date.

questions.prompt: A naïve RAG endpoint takes 1.5s. Requirement: sub-100ms latency. Walk through the plan.

rubric.criterion: Decomposes latency: tokenize, embed, vector search, prompt build, LLM inference, network
Applies caching: embed cache, response cache with semantic key, prefetch
Reduces LLM cost: smaller model, distillation, or answer-only classifier for FAQ path
Uses streaming to reduce time-to-first-token perception
Batches, KV-cache reuse, GPU/TPU choice, quantization
Acknowledges sub-100ms with an LLM in the loop is often impossible — proposes a cascading design

questions.modelAnswer: Break down: 30ms tokenize, 100ms embed, 200ms vector, 700ms LLM. Sub-100ms overall requires bypassing the LLM for common paths. Semantic-cache lookup first (edge-deployed). If miss, small-model classifier for FAQ intents. Only true novel queries hit the LLM (async streaming). Precompute embeddings for query templates. Colocate embedding model + vector DB. Set p50 SLO for cached path <50ms; be honest that novel-query p50 will be ~500ms streamed.

questions.prompt: A client's existing system is a 15-year-old on-premise ERP with no API layer. Design an integration.

rubric.criterion: Asks about DB access, batch export windows, existing extract processes
Doesn't propose an invasive rewrite — respects change control
Extraction strategy: read replica, CDC, file drops, screen-scrape as last resort
Transform + landing in modern data layer (S3/Snowflake), with schema versioning
Two-way sync considerations + conflict handling
Security + audit + rollback plan

questions.modelAnswer: Ask about DB engine and whether we can attach a read replica. Prefer: CDC via Debezium reading from replica → Kafka → S3/warehouse. Fallback: nightly SQL exports as CSV to SFTP. For writes: if ERP has import files, submit through their batch window; otherwise scope a thin adapter service that talks to whatever RPC/DB access is authorized. Everything auditable. Change-management flags every deploy.

questions.prompt: Design prompt versioning, A/B testing, and rollback in production.

rubric.criterion: Prompts as versioned artifacts (git or DB with immutable IDs)
Traffic-splitting infra (feature flag / experiment platform) with per-user sticky assignment
Metrics: task success rate, user thumbs-up/down, cost/latency deltas
Offline eval set replay before rollout
Fast rollback: single flag flip; last-known-good pinned
Audit: log which prompt version served which response for reproducibility

questions.modelAnswer: Prompts live in git as YAML with semantic versions. Deploy loads them into a Prompt Registry (DB + cache). Requests carry prompt_id/version. LaunchDarkly assigns users to variants; per-user hash for stickiness. Every response logs prompt_version + inputs + score. Weekly report: cohort success rates + cost. Rollback = disable flag. Offline eval on golden set runs on every PR affecting prompts.

questions.prompt: Design a caching strategy for a read-heavy product-catalog API (100k RPS, 10M products, updates once per hour).

rubric.criterion: Multi-layer: CDN edge → in-memory app cache → Redis → DB
Invalidation strategy: TTL + explicit purge on update; versioned cache keys
Cache-aside vs write-through choice with rationale
Hot-key + thundering-herd mitigation (request coalescing / stale-while-revalidate)
Metrics: hit ratio per layer, evictions, p99 tail

questions.modelAnswer: CDN caches full JSON per product for 5 min. App uses SWR with 30s freshness. Redis L2 with 1-hour TTL. Cache key includes catalog version so cutover is atomic. On product update: bump version + explicit CDN purge for changed IDs. Coalesce back-fills with sync.Once/singleflight to prevent stampede on cache-miss on hot IDs.

questions.prompt: Design observability for an AI agent system (LLM calls + tool use + state) that a client's ops team must run.

rubric.criterion: Traces every agent step (LLM call, tool call, retry) with trace + span ids
Log inputs, outputs, and prompt versions for reproducibility; PII redaction
Metrics: task success rate, LLM cost per task, tool failure rate, latency P95
Live dashboards + on-call alert rules on burn rates
Replay tooling: recreate a bad run from stored inputs
Client-visible view for their ops team, not just our engineers

questions.modelAnswer: OpenTelemetry spans per agent step. Langfuse or Arize AI for LLM-specific tracing (prompt/response/cost). Grafana dashboards for cost + success. Golden-run replayer that hydrates trace payloads to reproduce failures. Client-facing lightweight UI showing recent runs + drill-down.

questions.prompt: Design a webhook INGESTION engine handling 100k requests/sec with per-tenant rate limiting, retry backoffs, and tenant isolation. (The canonical Turing FDE Stage 4 prompt.)

rubric.criterion: Clarifies: are we the sender or receiver? What's the durability SLA? What ordering guarantees per tenant?
Front door: API Gateway / LB (nginx or ALB) with TLS termination, HMAC signature verification, sync 2xx ASAP
Ingest is a THIN handler: validate + write to durable queue (Kafka partitioned by tenant_id) and 202 back
Separate consumer fleet processes; auto-scales on queue depth per tenant partition
Per-tenant rate limit at edge (token bucket in Redis) + per-tenant queue quotas (backpressure surfaces as 429)
Retry with exp backoff + jitter, capped attempts, DLQ + replay tool
Tenant isolation: separate queue partitions (or separate topics), per-tenant worker pools OR bulkhead capacity
Idempotency key from sender + dedup store (Redis SET with TTL)
Observability: golden signals per tenant, alert on ingest failure rate, DLQ depth, consumer lag
Capacity math: 100k/sec × ~1KB = 100MB/s → 8.6TB/day → sizing Kafka + replication + retention

questions.modelAnswer: Edge: ALB → nginx (TLS, HMAC verify, rate limit per tenant via Redis Lua) → 3-tier fleet of ingest pods. Ingest pods do: (1) parse header, (2) verify HMAC, (3) check idempotency key in Redis (SETNX with 24h TTL), (4) write to Kafka topic `wh-events`, partitioned by tenant_id (~256 partitions), (5) return 202 with ID. Consumer fleet: per-tenant consumer groups, workers scale on lag (KEDA). Each worker processes with retry (5 attempts, exp backoff, jitter). Terminal failure → DLQ Kafka topic `wh-dlq` with error context + retryable flag. Ops UI to replay from DLQ. Per-tenant quotas enforced at edge (tokens/sec) and at consumer level (max in-flight per tenant). Sizing: 100k RPS × 1KB = 100MB/s → 6 brokers with RF=3 → ~150GB/hour → 7-day retention = ~25TB. Monitor: ingest 5xx rate, HMAC failures, per-tenant lag, DLQ depth. Alerts: >0.1% failure or lag > 5m. Golden path: end-to-end median <50ms; DLQ replay tool with dry-run mode.

questions.prompt: Design an active-active multi-region API with strong per-user consistency (a user always reads their own writes) but tolerant of one region failing.

rubric.criterion: Route users to home region (geo-DNS + user cookie for stickiness after failover)
Each region owns a slice of users (avoids cross-region write contention)
Global data (catalog, config) uses master-in-one-region + async read replicas
Failover: promote a healthy region to serve the failed region's users; RPO/RTO stated
Cross-region latency budget accounted for (writes to home region only; reads local)
Observability: per-region SLO + cross-region replication lag alerts
Data-residency / compliance considerations (EU users stay in EU)

questions.modelAnswer: Home-region-per-user pattern: user profile stores home_region; global service directory (Route 53 latency + failover) sends the user to home region. Home region owns writes for that user + async replica in disaster region. Failover flow: health checks flip DNS to disaster region; disaster promotes replica → primary; users may see 30-60s of writes replayed as replication catches up (documented RPO). Global catalog (products, config) has a leader region + eventual read replicas in each region. Latency SLO stated per region. Compliance: EU users pinned to EU home; disaster is another EU region.

questions.prompt: A client requires SAML SSO from their Okta and only allows their employees to reach your app. Design.

rubric.criterion: SP-initiated flow: user → app → redirect to Okta with SAMLRequest → Okta auth → SAMLResponse POST back → we validate signature + issuer + audience + not-before/not-on-or-after
Store Okta metadata (public cert, IdP entity ID) per tenant; support cert rotation
Map SAML attributes → our user model (email, groups → roles)
JIT provisioning: first SAML login creates the user record
SLO (Single Logout) support, or clear communication that we do only local logout
SCIM for user lifecycle (deprovision on offboarding)
Tenant-restricted subdomain / IdP-selection page so login lands on the right IdP

questions.modelAnswer: Multi-tenant. Login page routes by email domain to the tenant's IdP config or shows a picker at `/sso/select`. Use `saml2-js` or `passport-saml`. Per-tenant record: {sp_entity_id, idp_entity_id, idp_x509_cert, callback_url}. On response: validate signature, issuer, audience, timing, replay (store InResponseTo). Attributes → user: `NameID` → email, `groups` → roles. JIT: if no user, create. Optional SCIM v2 endpoint for Okta to POST provisioning events. Certificate rotation: support multiple valid certs simultaneously during rollover.

questions.prompt: Design product search over 5M items: filters, facets, typeahead, ranking. Traffic 5k QPS peak.

rubric.criterion: Choose search engine (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch/Meilisearch/Typesense) with rationale
Indexing pipeline: CDC from Postgres → transform → bulk index, incremental updates
Query design: bool query with must (text) + filter (facets) + sort (ranking); highlight
Typeahead via edge n-grams + separate lighter index, aggressive cache
Ranking: BM25 + business signals (popularity, freshness, revenue-weight) via function score
Multi-tenancy / geography / language shards
SLO: P95 <150ms; alert on latency + relevance regression

questions.modelAnswer: OpenSearch cluster, 3 data + 3 master, 5-shard 1-replica index. Debezium CDC from `products` table → Kafka → indexer service transforms + bulks. Query: `bool { must: multi_match(title, description) filter: {terms: {category, brand}, range: {price}} function_score: {popularity, freshness}}`. Typeahead: `products_suggest` index with completion suggester. Redis in front for suggest cache. Golden dataset of top 500 queries with expected ordering; nightly ranking eval. Auto-scale ingest workers on Kafka lag.

questions.prompt: Design a real-time analytics dashboard: 500k events/sec ingest, sub-second aggregations for 100 active dashboards.

rubric.criterion: Kafka ingest + Flink (or Materialize/RisingWave) for stateful streaming aggregation
Sink to a fast time-series / columnar store (ClickHouse, Druid, Pinot) OR Redis for the hot cube
Dashboards subscribe via WebSocket or SSE to only their needed cubes
Windowing choice (tumbling / sliding / session) with watermarks for late events
Exactly-once via Kafka EOS + idempotent sink
Cost + retention tiering (hot in RAM, warm in ClickHouse, cold in S3)

questions.modelAnswer: Events → Kafka (100 partitions). Flink jobs compute 1s tumbling + 1m sliding aggregates. Sink hot windows to Redis; historical to ClickHouse. Dashboard server subscribes to relevant Redis keys + broadcasts via WebSocket to browsers. Watermarks tolerate 10s late events; late-late events emit correction records. Kafka EOS + ClickHouse ReplacingMergeTree for idempotency. Retention: 1h in Redis, 90d in ClickHouse, forever in S3 (parquet).

questions.prompt: Design a feature-flag system usable across 200 services and 5M end-users with <10ms flag evaluation.

rubric.criterion: Central admin UI + evaluation SDK per service (JS/Go/Python)
Flag configs pushed to edges (S3/CDN + polling OR streaming SSE)
Evaluation happens LOCALLY (in-process) using cached config — never remote-per-call
User targeting rules: percentage rollout via stable hash, attribute rules
Audit log every flag change; PR-review workflow for prod changes
Kill switch: single-flag disable in <30 sec globally
Analytics: flag exposure events streamed to warehouse for experiment analysis

questions.modelAnswer: Config service publishes flag manifest to S3 + CDN + Redis pub/sub. SDK polls every 30s + subscribes to pub/sub for instant kill switches. Evaluation is pure in-process. Targeting: `hash(userId + flagId) < rolloutPercentage`. Admin UI writes to Postgres; changes flow through PR review for prod. Audit trail in append-only table. Exposure events posted async to Kafka → warehouse for experiment stats.

questions.prompt: Design a notification service: email + SMS + push, 10M users, at-least-once, per-user preferences, deliverability.

rubric.criterion: API accepts logical notification → template renders per channel → provider adapter sends
Per-user preference store filters channels before send
Rate limits + digests to prevent spam
Provider failover (SendGrid → SES; Twilio → MessageBird) with weighted routing
Suppression list (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes) enforced on send
Delivery tracking (webhooks from provider → status update)
Observability: delivery rate, bounce rate, latency per channel + provider

questions.modelAnswer: Producers → Kafka topic per channel. Renderer service loads template + user prefs, renders per channel, checks suppression list, publishes to send queue. Sender workers per provider consume, apply per-provider rate limit (Redis token bucket), track message id. Provider webhooks land on webhook consumer that updates message status + suppression list. Preference UI writes to Postgres. Deliverability: SPF/DKIM/DMARC set up per sending domain; regular list hygiene.

questions.prompt: Design a chat system with 1:1 + group chats, presence, typing indicators, and 100k concurrent users.

rubric.criterion: WebSocket for real-time; REST for history; separate concerns
Message storage: Cassandra/DynamoDB partitioned by conversation_id + timestamp
Fan-out via Redis pub/sub across app nodes (per-conversation channel)
Presence: TTL keys in Redis, heartbeat every 30s
Typing: ephemeral events, NOT persisted
Media: signed upload URLs to object storage, only URL flows through chat
E2EE optional but designed for; keys never on server

questions.modelAnswer: WS server behind LB with sticky-by-user or Redis-backed connection registry. Per-conversation pub/sub channel; server node subscribes on behalf of connected clients. Cassandra table: `messages(conversation_id, sent_at, message_id, sender_id, body)`. Presence: `HSET presence user_id ts`, TTL 90s. Typing broadcasts through pub/sub but never stored. Client uploads media directly to S3 via pre-signed URLs.
